name: Claude Code v2.1.275 — Skills & Plugins Sync

Also ships a send-now key (ctrl+enter) that interrupts the current turn and flushes queued messages, plus `/plugin install --marketplace` for one-command marketplace adds. v2.1.276 (Sep 18) patches a proxy 400 regression introduced by 275.

Still the undisputed #1 COST tool in the ecosystem.

name: boss-skill
hook: 558 stars. Turns a single coding agent into a structured engineering team: PM, Architect, Designer, Tech Lead, and QA roles coordinate via event sourcing with quality gates and replayable artifacts. Every run produces a documented .boss/ folder (PRDs, architecture specs, code reviews, test reports) — auditability that pure prompt-based orchestration can't match. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, and Trae.

name: ARIS (Auto-Research-In-Sleep)
hook: 16.3K stars. 81-skill bundle for autonomous ML research: /research-pipeline runs end-to-end paper generation, /idea-discovery does five-stage brainstorming with a deterministic evidence gate, /rebuttal crafts reviewer responses, and /experiment-audit checks empirical rigor. Sep 16 update (v0.4.26) adds Fable 5.1 support, GPT-6-Astra as default reviewer, and codex-cli 0.154 compatibility.
recurring_note: Recurring — updated Sep 16 with Fable 5.1 support and GPT-6-Astra reviewer

name: EvoOntology
hook: 148 stars, created Sep 15. A self-evolving ontology layer for data agents that builds and refines a shared knowledge graph as your agent works — so terminology, schema names, and domain concepts are consistent across multi-step data pipelines. Installs as a Claude Code plugin or Codex skill; no external services required. Comes from a Chinese data-lab research group with a track record of agent-infrastructure papers.

name: jev-review
hook: 112 stars, created Sep 17 — the newest entry. A local-first MCP plugin powered by Jev (TypeSafe.ai) that runs continuous code-quality review inside your agent's loop: structural analysis, test coverage gaps, and style violations all flagged before a commit touches CI. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode. No cloud required; results live in your repo.

name: Friday — Persistent Cognitive Memory
hook: 36 stars, created Sep 16. Open-source alternative to the closed memory services: a Neo4j + FastAPI knowledge graph served over MCP that gives Claude, Cursor, and Copilot persistent memory across sessions. Stores entities, relationships, and observations extracted from conversations; query with natural language. Self-host in Docker in under five minutes. Explicitly bills itself as the fix for "AI agent amnesia."

name: VibeTube
hook: 58 stars, created Sep 15. macOS desktop app that records your screen + webcam in sync, then hands the raw footage to Claude Code or Codex for shot selection, auto-subtitles, graphics, and SFX — producing a polished final cut without touching a timeline editor. The agent gets a structured storyboard JSON and edits via ffmpeg. Targets devs who demo-to-YouTube but hate editing.

name: seanswarm
hook: 53 stars, created Sep 16. Three production-grade multi-agent workflow skills in one package: evidence-governed research fan-out (agents cite sources before aggregating), dual-channel document reading (primary + adversarial), and dev delivery with an independent reviewer agent that must approve before merge. Works across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor without framework lock-in.

name: skillranker
hook: 43 stars, created Sep 17 by Dicklesworthstone (well-known OSS prolific author). A Rust CLI powered by Jev that reads live session context and scores every installed skill for fit to the next step — so your agent picks the right skill instead of guessing. Includes Claude Code hooks for automatic injection, structured JSON output, and a local feedback loop. Requires a TypeSafe API key.

name: agent-router
hook: 25 stars, created Sep 17. A CLI that picks the right coding agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode) plus model and effort level for any given task — then launches it. Powered by Jev and Herdr for routing logic. Useful on multi-agent setups where token costs vary wildly by task type; saves money by routing cheap tasks to cheaper agents automatically.

name: GPUtw-Skill
hook: 52 stars, created Sep 15. Official skill from GPUtw.ai that teaches Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI to provision and manage GPUs via the GPUtw REST API — spin up cloud GPU instances, check availability, monitor jobs, and teardown from inside your agent session. Aimed at ML engineers who train models locally and need burst GPU capacity without leaving the terminal.

name: claude-code-mods
hook: 27 stars, created Sep 15, and its companion awesome-claude-code-mods (20 stars) is already the canonical index for the new category. "Mods" use Claude Code's function-hooks API to draw custom UI and register new tools the model can call — think Minecraft mods but for your coding agent. The builder skill scaffolds a new mod in minutes. First mods include a token meter, a diff annotator, and a session replay tool.

name: diagram-design
hook: 41.1K stars. 39 editorial-quality diagram types — architecture, flow, sequence, Gantt, state machines, pyramids, quadrants — delivered as self-contained HTML+SVG with three static variants (minimal light, minimal dark, full editorial). No Mermaid slop, no Figma required. v2.5.10 added 10 new layout types this week. Created by BestSelf.co founder Cathryn Lavery; used by design-focused teams shipping UI-rich projects with Claude Code.
recurring_note: Recurring — v2.5.10 adds 10 new layout types, still the top DESIGN skill

name: Statewright
hook: 491 stars. Define AI agent workflows as state machines — planning states get read-only tools, implementation unlocks edit access, testing permits only designated commands. Enforced at the protocol layer via MCP, not via prompt gymnastics. Works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi. Rust engine, Apache 2.0, free tier available. Plugin 0.3.3 improved native MCP read-only annotations and session management.
